I do not like people. They are too loud, too fast, too bright. I prefer the dark, the silence, the stillness. I hunt in the dark, I sleep in the dark, I live in the dark. People are not part of my world. I do not understand them. I do not trust them. I do not like them.

The oak. It stands tall and strong, and I can hear the wind through its leaves all night. The hollow in its trunk is my home, and the nuts fall to the ground below. I can hear the voles and mice moving through the roots. The oak is safe, and I am safe in it. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I stay in the hollow. The rain is loud and the wind is sharp, but the oak is strong and the ivy holds. I sit tight and listen. The storm is not my enemy. A fridge is a thing I have never seen. The word is not one I know. I have heard it in the lit of the barn, when the humans talk to each other.
